    The monarchs of Europe, having absorbed the knowledge of the ancient Greeks and Romans, had developed a sophisticated understanding of governance and economics. They had created a system of meritocracy, where the most skilled and talented individuals were rewarded with land, titles, and power.

    The nobility, once the sole beneficiaries of privilege and wealth, had been transformed into a class of enlightened leaders. They had taken on the role of patron and mentor, guiding the development of their subjects and fostering a culture of innovation and progress.

    The peasants, once bound to the land by feudal obligations, had been freed to pursue their passions and interests. They had formed guilds and cooperatives, working together to build thriving communities and industries.

    The cities, once centers of commerce and trade, had become hubs of cultural and intellectual activity. The universities, founded by the great minds of the past, had become centers of learning and discovery, attracting scholars and thinkers from across the world.

    The great empires of Asia, having absorbed the knowledge of the ancient Silk Road, had developed a sophisticated understanding of trade and diplomacy. They had established a network of alliances and trade agreements, connecting the East and West in a web of commerce and cooperation.

    The world was a place of wonder and discovery, where the boundaries between nations and cultures were blurred. The people lived in a state of constant evolution, adapting to the changing needs of their societies and the world around them.

    In this world, the concept of nation-states had given way to a more fluid and dynamic understanding of identity and belonging. The people were no longer bound by the strictures of nationality, but were free to move and work wherever their skills and talents were in demand.

    The Great Convergence had also brought about a new era of scientific and technological progress. The discovery of the printing press had spread knowledge and ideas across the world, fueling a period of rapid innovation and discovery.
